format: Text with inline TeX in $...$ and display TeX in $$...$$. Answer label and value fields are TeX without delimiters.

problems.title: Derive the second telegrapher's equation
problems.prompt: Using the lumped-element model of a transmission line (series $R'\Delta z$ and $L'\Delta z$, shunt $G'\Delta z$ and $C'\Delta z$), apply KCL to derive$$-\frac{\partial i(z,t)}{\partial z}=G'v(z,t)+C'\frac{\partial v(z,t)}{\partial t}$$
hints: Write KCL at the node after the series elements: the current in equals the current through the shunt branch plus the current continuing down the line.
The shunt branch current is $G'\Delta z\,v + C'\Delta z\,\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial t}$.
Divide by $\Delta z$ and take the limit $\Delta z\to 0$.
steps: KCL at the node at $z+\Delta z$:$$i(z,t)=i(z+\Delta z,t)+i_{\mathrm{shunt}}$$
The shunt current is$$i_{\mathrm{shunt}}=G'\Delta z\,v(z+\Delta z,t)+C'\Delta z\,\frac{\partial v(z+\Delta z,t)}{\partial t}$$
Rearrange and divide by $\Delta z$:$$-\frac{i(z+\Delta z,t)-i(z,t)}{\Delta z}=G'v(z+\Delta z,t)+C'\frac{\partial v(z+\Delta z,t)}{\partial t}$$
Let $\Delta z\to 0$. The left side becomes $-\dfrac{\partial i}{\partial z}$ and $v(z+\Delta z)\to v(z)$:$$-\frac{\partial i(z,t)}{\partial z}=G'v(z,t)+C'\frac{\partial v(z,t)}{\partial t}$$

problems.title: Wave equation for the current
problems.prompt: Using the phasor telegrapher's equations, derive the governing equation for $I(z)$ on a lossy line, define $\gamma$, and give the solution for the lossless case. Identify the real and imaginary parts of $\gamma=\alpha+j\beta$.
hints: The phasor forms are $-\dfrac{dV}{dz}=(R'+j\omega L')I$ and $-\dfrac{dI}{dz}=(G'+j\omega C')V$.
Differentiate the second equation with respect to $z$ and substitute the first.
problems.note: The course answer key writes $I_0^+ + e^{-j\beta z}$; the plus sign between the amplitude and the exponential is a typo.

problems.title: Verify the wave solution
problems.prompt: Show that $\tilde V(z)=V_0^+e^{-\gamma z}+V_0^-e^{\gamma z}$ solves$$\frac{d^2\tilde V}{dz^2}-\gamma^2\tilde V=0$$

problems.title: Wave speed in a dielectric
problems.prompt: A wave travels in a material with relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r=5$. What is its speed?

problems.title: Input impedance of a 1.5λ line
problems.prompt: A lossless $50\ \Omega$ line, $1.5\lambda$ long, is terminated in $72+j42\ \Omega$. What is the input impedance?
hints: What is $\tan\beta\ell$ when $\ell$ is a multiple of $\lambda/2$?
steps: A half-wavelength line repeats the load impedance.
problems.note: The course solution substitutes $72+j45\ \Omega$ in one line; the load is $72+j42\ \Omega$.

problems.title: When is $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ purely real?
problems.prompt: A lossless $50\ \Omega$ coax is terminated in $25+j25\ \Omega$. (a) Plot $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ in the complex plane for $\ell$ from $0$ to $0.45\lambda$. (b) For what lengths is $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ purely real, and what is $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ there?
hints: $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ is real where the point on the Smith chart crosses the real axis.
Those crossings are the voltage maximum and minimum positions.

problems.title: Open-circuited coax at 900 MHz
problems.prompt: A $13\ \mathrm{cm}$ section of $75\ \Omega$ coax is open at the far end. With velocity factor $0.55$, what is the input impedance at $900\ \mathrm{MHz}$?
problems.note: The course key gives $-j19.26\ \Omega$ because $\ell$ is rounded to $0.71\lambda$; carrying full precision gives $-j19.47\ \Omega$.

problems.title: Reading a traveling wave
problems.prompt: A voltage on a lossless line is$$v(z,t)=5\cos\!\left(4\pi\times10^{9}\,t-60z\right)\ \mathrm{V}$$Find the frequency, $\beta$, the phase velocity, the wavelength, and the relative permittivity of the dielectric.
steps: The wave travels in $+z$ because $\omega t$ and $\beta z$ have opposite signs.

problems.title: Line constants from L′ and C′
problems.prompt: A lossless line has $L'=300\ \mathrm{nH/m}$ and $C'=120\ \mathrm{pF/m}$. At $500\ \mathrm{MHz}$, find $Z_0$, $u_p$, $\beta$, and $\lambda$.

problems.title: A lossy line at 50 MHz
problems.prompt: A line has $R'=2\ \Omega/\mathrm{m}$, $L'=250\ \mathrm{nH/m}$, $G'=0.5\ \mathrm{mS/m}$, and $C'=100\ \mathrm{pF/m}$. At $50\ \mathrm{MHz}$, find $\gamma$, $\alpha$ in dB/m, $\beta$, and $Z_0$. How much does a wave's amplitude drop over $20\ \mathrm{m}$?
hints: The amplitude ratio over a length $\ell$ is $e^{-\alpha\ell}$.

problems.title: Input impedance at 0.18λ
problems.prompt: Find the input impedance of a $0.18\lambda$ length of $50\ \Omega$ line terminated in $40+j70\ \Omega$. Check your answer on the Smith chart.
hints: On the Smith chart, rotate $0.18\lambda$ toward the generator.
steps: Smith chart: $z_L=0.8+j1.4$ sits at $0.166\lambda$ WTG. Moving $0.18\lambda$ lands at $0.346\lambda$ WTG.

problems.title: A shorted stub that acts like an inductor
problems.prompt: At $2.4\ \mathrm{GHz}$ you need $+j100\ \Omega$ from a shorted $50\ \Omega$ stub with $u_p=0.7c$. What is the shortest stub length, in wavelengths and millimeters? What inductor would give the same reactance?

problems.title: An open stub that acts like a capacitor
problems.prompt: What is the shortest length of open-circuited $50\ \Omega$ line that looks like a $2\ \mathrm{pF}$ capacitor at $1\ \mathrm{GHz}$?

problems.title: Generator, line and load
problems.prompt: A $12\ \mathrm{V}$ (amplitude) source with $50\ \Omega$ internal impedance drives a $0.35\lambda$, $50\ \Omega$ lossless line terminated in $25-j40\ \Omega$. Find $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$, $V_{\mathrm{in}}$, $V_0^+$, the load voltage, and the average power delivered to the load.
hints: Find $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ first, then use a voltage divider at the input.
$V(z)=V_0^+\left(e^{-j\beta z}+\Gamma_Le^{j\beta z}\right)$; evaluate it at $z=-\ell$ to find $V_0^+$.
On a lossless line, all the power entering the line reaches the load.
steps: $|V_0^+|=6\ \mathrm{V}$ because $Z_s=Z_0$: the source launches $V_s/2$ whatever the load.

problems.title: Mismatched at both ends
problems.prompt: A $20\ \mathrm{V}$ source with $75\ \Omega$ internal resistance drives a $0.2\lambda$, $50\ \Omega$ line terminated in $150\ \Omega$. Find $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ and the power delivered to the load, and compare it with the source's available power $\dfrac{V_s^2}{8R_s}$.
hints: Find $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ first, then treat the input as a voltage divider.
Available power is what a conjugate-matched load would get.
steps: $$P_{\mathrm{avail}}=\frac{20^2}{8(75)}=667\ \mathrm{mW}$$The load receives $61.4\%$ of the available power.

problems.title: Reflected voltage wave
problems.prompt: A $7\ \mathrm{mV}\angle 180^\circ$ voltage wave travels on a lossless $60\ \Omega$ line terminated in a $20\ \Omega$ load. Find the magnitude and phase of the reflected wave.
hints: $\Gamma_L$ is real and negative here, which adds $180^\circ$.
problems.note: The course solution writes $\Gamma_L=\dfrac{Z_L-Z_0}{Z_L-Z_0}$; the denominator should be $Z_L+Z_0$.

problems.title: Γ and VSWR for a 60 Ω load on a 72 Ω line
problems.prompt: A $72\ \Omega$ line is terminated in a $60\ \Omega$ load. (a) Sketch the system. (b) Find $\Gamma_L$. (c) Find the VSWR.
hints: Put the load at $z=0$ and the input at $z=-\ell$.

problems.title: Γ, VSWR and impedance at z = −0.3λ
problems.prompt: A lossless $50\ \Omega$ line is terminated in $Z_L=20-j35\ \Omega$. Find (a) $\Gamma_L$, (b) the VSWR, and (c) the impedance at $z=-0.3\lambda$.
problems.note: The course solution shows $|\Gamma|=0.636$ in an intermediate step; it should be $0.589$. The final answer is unaffected.

problems.title: Where are the peaks and nulls?
problems.prompt: A $75\ \Omega$ line is terminated in $30+j45\ \Omega$. Find $\Gamma_L$, the VSWR, and the distances from the load to the first voltage maximum and minimum.
hints: Voltage maxima occur where the phase of $\Gamma(d)=\Gamma_Le^{-j2\beta d}$ is zero.

problems.title: Reflected and transmitted voltage
problems.prompt: An incident wave $V_0^+=4\ \mathrm{V}\angle 30^\circ$ on a $50\ \Omega$ line reaches a $100-j100\ \Omega$ load. Find the reflected wave $V_0^-$ and the load voltage $V_L$.

problems.title: Reading a VNA return loss
problems.prompt: A VNA shows a return loss of $14\ \mathrm{dB}$ ($S_{11}=-14\ \mathrm{dB}$) for an antenna on a $50\ \Omega$ system. What are $|\Gamma|$, the VSWR, and the fraction of incident power reflected?

problems.title: Find the load from standing-wave measurements
problems.prompt: On a $50\ \Omega$ line you measure $\mathrm{VSWR}=3$, with the first voltage minimum $0.12\lambda$ from the load. What is $Z_L$?
hints: At a voltage minimum the phase of $\Gamma(d)$ is $-180^\circ$, so $\theta_\Gamma-\dfrac{4\pi d_{\mathrm{min}}}{\lambda}=-\pi$.
steps: Smith chart check: start at the $V_{\mathrm{min}}$ point ($z=1/3$ on the real axis) and rotate $0.12\lambda$ toward the load.

problems.title: Series element match without a Smith chart
problems.prompt: Without a Smith chart, match a $35-j50\ \Omega$ load to a $100\ \Omega$ source at $1\ \mathrm{GHz}$ using a length $\ell$ of $100\ \Omega$ line followed by a series reactive element. Find $\ell$ and the element value for (a) a series capacitor and (b) a series inductor.
hints: Find $\ell$ where $\mathrm{Re}\{z_{\mathrm{in}}\}=1$ using the transmission-line equation, normalized to $100\ \Omega$.
A capacitor cancels positive reactance; an inductor cancels negative reactance.
steps: (a) $\mathrm{Re}\{z_{\mathrm{in}}\}=1$ at $\ell=0.254\lambda$, where $z_{\mathrm{in}}=1+j1.39$. The capacitor must provide $-j138.6\ \Omega$:$$C=\frac{1}{\omega X}=\frac{1}{2\pi(10^9)(138.6)}=1.15\ \mathrm{pF}$$

(b) $\mathrm{Re}\{z_{\mathrm{in}}\}=1$ at $\ell=0.407\lambda$, where $z_{\mathrm{in}}=1-j1.39$. The inductor must provide $+j138.6\ \Omega$:$$L=\frac{X}{\omega}=\frac{138.6}{2\pi(10^9)}=22.1\ \mathrm{nH}$$
problems.note: The course key lists $L=221\ \mu\mathrm{H}$. At $1\ \mathrm{GHz}$ a $139\ \Omega$ reactance needs $22.1\ \mathrm{nH}$, so $\mu\mathrm{H}$ appears to be a units slip.

problems.title: Four ways to match 35 − j50 Ω with a Smith chart
problems.prompt: Using a Smith chart, match a $35-j50\ \Omega$ load to a $100\ \Omega$ source at $1\ \mathrm{GHz}$ with a length of $100\ \Omega$ line and one reactive element: (a) series capacitor, (b) series inductor, (c) shunt capacitor, (d) shunt inductor.
hints: Series elements: rotate on the Z chart to the $r=1$ circle.
Shunt elements: convert to admittance and rotate to the $g=1$ circle.
Read the leftover reactance or susceptance and pick the element that cancels it.
steps: Plot $z_L=0.35-j0.5$ and draw its VSWR circle ($\mathrm{VSWR}=3.65$).
(c) On the Y chart, reach $g=1$ at $\ell=0.157\lambda$: $y=1-j1.39$. A shunt capacitor supplies $B=1.39/100\ \mathrm{S}$:$$C=\frac{B}{\omega}=2.21\ \mathrm{pF}$$
(d) Reach $g=1$ at $\ell=0.0036\lambda$: $y=1+j1.39$. A shunt inductor cancels it:$$L=\frac{1}{\omega B}=11.5\ \mathrm{nH}$$
problems.note: The course key gives $L=221.2\ \mu\mathrm{H}$ for (b) and $113.7\ \mu\mathrm{H}$ for (d). The reactances at $1\ \mathrm{GHz}$ correspond to $22.1\ \mathrm{nH}$ and $11.5\ \mathrm{nH}$.

problems.title: 170 Ω load: quarter-wave transformer and shorted stub
problems.prompt: Match a $170\ \Omega$ load to a $50\ \Omega$ source. (a) What characteristic impedance does a quarter-wave transformer need? (b) Using $50\ \Omega$ line, find the through-line length and shorted shunt-stub length.
hints: For the stub, work in admittance: $y_L=\dfrac{50}{170}$.
Rotate $y_L$ toward the generator until it meets the $g=1$ circle.
steps: Solution 1: at $d=0.171\lambda$, $y=1+j1.30$. The shorted stub must add $-j1.30$, so $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}=0.104\lambda$.
Solution 2: at $d=0.329\lambda$, $y=1-j1.30$. The shorted stub must add $+j1.30$, so $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}=0.396\lambda$.
problems.note: The course key lists $y_{\mathrm{stub}}=\pm j1.07$ with $d=0.086\lambda$ and $0.4125\lambda$. For a $170\ \Omega$ load on $50\ \Omega$ line the $g=1$ crossings are at $1\pm j1.30$, which gives the values here.

problems.title: Open shunt stub for 200 + j160 Ω
problems.prompt: Match $Z_L=200+j160\ \Omega$ to a $100\ \Omega$ source with an open shunt stub on $100\ \Omega$ line. Find the solution with the shortest stub.
hints: Find both $g=1$ crossings, compute both stub lengths, and keep the shorter one.
steps: At $d=0.213\lambda$: $y=1+j1.33$, so the open stub is $\ell=0.352\lambda$.
At $d=0.370\lambda$: $y=1-j1.33$, so the open stub is $\ell=0.148\lambda$.
The shortest open stub is $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}=0.148\lambda$ with $d=0.370\lambda$.

problems.title: Shorted shunt stub for 200 + j160 Ω
problems.prompt: Repeat the previous problem with a shorted shunt stub. Find the solution with the shortest stub.
hints: The two $g=1$ crossings are the same as before; only the stub length changes.
steps: At $d=0.213\lambda$ the stub must supply $-j1.33$, so the shorted stub is $\ell=0.102\lambda$.
At $d=0.370\lambda$ the stub must supply $+j1.33$, so the shorted stub is $\ell=0.398\lambda$.
The shortest shorted stub is $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}=0.102\lambda$ with $d=0.213\lambda$.
problems.note: The course key gives $d=0.221\lambda$ and $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}=0.100\lambda$, which agree with these values to Smith-chart reading accuracy.

problems.title: Quarter-wave transformer
problems.prompt: Match a $300\ \Omega$ antenna to a $75\ \Omega$ line at $600\ \mathrm{MHz}$ with a quarter-wave transformer built on a dielectric with $\varepsilon_r=2.2$. Find $Z_1$ and the physical length.
steps: The match is exact only at $600\ \mathrm{MHz}$; at other frequencies the section is no longer $\lambda/4$.

problems.title: Quarter-wave transformer for a complex load
problems.prompt: A $60+j40\ \Omega$ load sits on a $50\ \Omega$ line. A quarter-wave transformer only matches real impedances. Find where on the line to insert it (at a voltage maximum or minimum) and the $Z_1$ needed in each case.
hints: At a voltage maximum the line impedance is real and equals $Z_0\cdot\mathrm{VSWR}$.
At a voltage minimum it is real and equals $\dfrac{Z_0}{\mathrm{VSWR}}$.

problems.title: Shorted shunt stub for 30 − j40 Ω
problems.prompt: Design a shorted shunt-stub match for $Z_L=30-j40\ \Omega$ on $50\ \Omega$ line. Give both solutions ($d$ and $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}$).
hints: Rotate on the VSWR circle until $g=1$.
steps: Solution 1: at $d=0.0417\lambda$, $y=1+j1.15$. The stub adds $-j1.15$, so $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}=0.114\lambda$.
Solution 2: at $d=0.208\lambda$, $y=1-j1.15$. The stub adds $+j1.15$, so $\ell_{\mathrm{stub}}=0.386\lambda$.

problems.title: Series element match at 2 GHz
problems.prompt: Match $Z_L=100+j80\ \Omega$ to $50\ \Omega$ at $2\ \mathrm{GHz}$ using a length of $50\ \Omega$ line followed by a series lumped element. Give both solutions, each with its element type and value.
hints: Cancel the leftover reactance with a capacitor if it is $+jx$, or an inductor if it is $-jx$.

problems.title: Bounce diagram: 30 Ω source, 150 Ω load
problems.prompt: A $10\ \mathrm{V}$ step source with $30\ \Omega$ internal resistance drives an $8\ \mathrm{cm}$, $50\ \Omega$ line ($u_p=0.67c$) terminated in $150\ \Omega$. (a) Draw the bounce diagram. Sketch the voltage out to $2\ \mathrm{ns}$ at (b) the source end, (c) the midpoint, and (d) the load.
hints: Each new wave is the previous one times $\Gamma_L$ or $\Gamma_s$.
steps: Source end: $6.250\ \mathrm{V}$ for $0<t<2T$, then $8.594\ \mathrm{V}$, then $8.301\ \mathrm{V}$ after $4T$.

problems.title: Step response on a 300 m line
problems.prompt: A $12\ \mathrm{V}$ step with $25\ \Omega$ source resistance drives a $300\ \mathrm{m}$, $75\ \Omega$ line ($u_p=2\times10^8\ \mathrm{m/s}$) terminated in $225\ \Omega$. Find $T$, $\Gamma_s$, $\Gamma_L$, and $V_L$ at $t=2$, $5$, and $8\ \mu\mathrm{s}$. What is the steady-state load voltage?
hints: The load first sees the incident wave plus its own reflection at $t=T$.

problems.title: Open-circuited line
problems.prompt: A $9\ \mathrm{V}$ step source with $150\ \Omega$ resistance is connected to an open-circuited $50\ \Omega$ line with one-way delay $T$. Sketch the voltage at the source end from $0$ to $6T$ and say where it settles.
hints: The source-end voltage only changes at $t=0,\,2T,\,4T,\dots$
steps: It climbs toward $9\ \mathrm{V}$: with no load current, nothing drops across $R_s$.
